svg.aria-label: Four spec tiles for a twelve dollar a month virtual machine: one vCPU on a shared core at 2.0 gigahertz, two gigabytes of RAM of which 1,967 megabytes are usable, a fifty gigabyte solid state disk against a database of only 349 megabytes, and a billed rate of 0.018 dollars per hour. The caption points out that the word doing the most work in the specification is shared, because a shared core is not a guaranteed core, and that advertised memory and usable memory are different numbers.

svg.text: The word doing the most work in that specification is shared.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: A shared core is not a guaranteed core, so every CPU figure later sits on a ceiling that can move.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Note the second gap: 2 GB advertised presents as 1,967 MB usable. Use the second number.

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The disk is 140x larger than the data on it, which is why storage never appears again.
